rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Authority often hides inside delivery.

GAME MOVE
Start Read Wrong; use Keep Words. Let Replay finish.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Read Wrong — Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep Words — Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Replay — Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Replay, then return to your day.

GAME MOVE
Start Project; use Move Metres. Do not pass Read Version.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Project — Project the sentence on an inner screen.
2. Shrink — Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move Metres — Move it two metres away.
4. Lower Opacity — Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read Version — Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.

GAME MOVE
Enter at State Fact; turn at Remove Approval. Final beat: Add Nothing.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. State Fact — State the fact in plain past or present tense.
2. Remove Approval — Remove approval, blame, and every ‘should not have happened.’ Notice the body’s protest and answer, ‘Not liking it is allowed.
3. Add Nothing — Refusing its existence adds nothing.’ Choose the next response available in the world that actually exists.

FINISH MOVE — Add Nothing is your cue to stop.

rituals.game_move: Choose Genuinely first. Details carries the middle. Do not pass Afterward.
rituals.unique_game_move: Choose Genuinely first. Details carries the middle. Do not pass Afterward.

TRIGGER
Emotional reasoning

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Put Good On The Calendar interrupts Emotion–fact confusion. Work toward: Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Positive events need appointments, not vague hope.

GAME MOVE
Choose Genuinely first. Details carries the middle. Do not pass Afterward.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Genuinely — Choose one genuinely reinforcing experience; assign it a time, place, and first action.
2. Protect Appointment — Protect the appointment from unnecessary multitasking.
3. Details — While it happens, notice three details worth encoding.
4. Afterward — Afterward, resist grading whether you enjoyed it ‘enough.’

TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Borrow The Sensation interrupts Body-sensation misinterpretation. Finish criterion: Teach the body that a safe signal is not worst-case story.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Teach the body that a safe signal is not worst-case story.

GAME MOVE
Select Medically first. Test Sensation carries the middle. Last decision: Test Sensation.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Select Medically — Select a medically safe exercise that creates a mild feared sensation—brief spinning, stair walking, or breathing through a narrow straw only when appropriate.
2. Test Sensation — Predict what will happen, induce the sensation briefly, and observe recovery without usual calming it.

FINISH MOVE — Test Sensation closes the round.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Borrow The Sensation works if this shifts: teach the body that a safe signal is not worst-case story. Keep evidence; leave at Test Sensation.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Medically → Test Sensation

rituals.title: THE RETURN REP
rituals.name: THE RETURN REP
rituals.hook: The Return Rep tests Perfectionism directly. Hold this purpose: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.recognition_cue: The Return Rep tests Perfectionism directly. Hold this purpose: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.goal: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.mission: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.challenge: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.immediate_need: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.game_move: Use Select Neutral; work through Count Rather. Leave it at End After.
rituals.unique_game_move: Use Select Neutral; work through Count Rather. Leave it at End After.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
The Return Rep tests Perfectionism directly. Hold this purpose: Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay.

GAME MOVE
Use Select Neutral; work through Count Rather. Leave it at End After.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Select Neutral — Select one neutral anchor.
2. Attention — Each time distraction appears, notice where attention went and escort it back without commentary.
3. Count Rather — Count returns rather than uninterrupted seconds.
4. End After — End after ten honest comebacks, even if focus never felt perfect.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The Return Rep gives one sign: attention strengthens on the comeback, not the stay. Do not grade End After.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Neutral → Attention → Count Rather → End After
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Choose a broader practice if narrow focus increases agitation.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.safety_notes:

rituals.hook: Bring Let Darkness Be Complete to Attention misallocation. Keep this aim: Visual absence does not need a replacement image.

rituals.mission: Visual absence does not need a replacement image.

rituals.unique_game_move: 3 moves: Set Darkness into Return Unfilled. Let Stay Briefly finish.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Bring Let Darkness Be Complete to Attention misallocation. Keep this aim: Visual absence does not need a replacement image.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Visual absence does not need a replacement image.

GAME MOVE
3 moves: Set Darkness into Return Unfilled. Let Stay Briefly finish.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Set Darkness — In a safe darkened setting, notice darkness as the actual visual field.
2. Return Unfilled — When the mind manufactures shapes or stories, recognise image production and return to the unfilled field.
3. Stay Briefly — Stay briefly, then reintroduce light on purpose.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL

rituals.formula_flow: Set Darkness → Return Unfilled → Stay Briefly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this practice if darkness triggers panic, trauma, or perceptual disturbance.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

HOOK
Bring Before The Sentence to Attention misallocation. Use this target: Look for thought at the moment of assembly.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Look for thought at the moment of assembly.

GAME MOVE
4 moves: Hold Attention into No Backtracking. Exit at Birth.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Hold Attention — Hold attention quietly and wait.
2. Earliest — When a thought begins, notice its earliest form: pressure, fragment, image, word, or sense of where you are.
3. No Backtracking — Do not chase backward after it fully forms.
4. Birth — Simply Notice ‘birth’ and let the completed thought continue.

FINISH MOVE — Birth closes the round.

GOAL
Diversity need not become division.

GAME MOVE
Contrasting frames it; Include Shared tests it. Do not pass Let Difference.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Contrasting — Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence.
2. Hold Distinct — Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
3. Include Shared — Then include the shared field in which both are present.
4. Let Difference — Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Let Difference, then return to your day.

GAME MOVE
Start at Describe Event; next, Watch Behaviour. After Ask Future, return.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Describe Event — Say the event from your position.
2. Move Seats — Move seats and say what the other person might perceive, labelling guesses.
3. Watch Behaviour — Stand as a neutral observer and Keep behaviour only.
4. Ask Future — Finally, ask what future-you would wish had happened next.

FINISH MOVE — Ask Future is your cue to stop.

rituals.hook: Move The Heaviest Word challenges Body-state misreading briefly. Keep the task narrow: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.recognition_cue: Move The Heaviest Word challenges Body-state misreading briefly. Keep the task narrow: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.goal: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.mission: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.challenge: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.immediate_need: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.game_move: Start at Say Alarm; next, Find Weight. Stopping line: Keep Signal.
rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Say Alarm; next, Find Weight. Stopping line: Keep Signal.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Move The Heaviest Word challenges Body-state misreading briefly. Keep the task narrow: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.

GAME MOVE
Start at Say Alarm; next, Find Weight. Stopping line: Keep Signal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.

FINISH MOVE — Keep Signal is your cue to stop.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The practical win in Move The Heaviest Word: move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight. End at Keep Signal.
rituals.formula_flow: Say Alarm → Shift Stress → Find Weight → Keep Signal
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use silent emphasis if speaking is unsafe; stop for voice strain, breathing difficulty, or rising panic.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
rituals.name: A PLACE FOR THE LOSS
rituals.hook: A Place For The Loss challenges Grief resistance briefly. Let this change: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.recognition_cue: A Place For The Loss challenges Grief resistance briefly. Let this change: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.goal: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.mission: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.challenge: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.immediate_need: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.game_move: Start at Choose Object; next, Say Name. Close Bond arrives; experiment over.
rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Choose Object; next, Say Name. Close Bond arrives; experiment over.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
A Place For The Loss challenges Grief resistance briefly. Let this change: Grief needs a deliberate address in time.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grief needs a deliberate address in time.

GAME MOVE
Start at Choose Object; next, Say Name. Close Bond arrives; experiment over.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Choose Object — Choose an object, date, location, and act of remembrance.
2. Say Name — Say the name of what was lost, honour what remains meaningful, and Notice a farewell to what cannot continue.
3. Close Bond — Close by deciding how the bond or value will be carried forward.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Grief needs a deliberate address in time. When A Place For The Loss reaches Close Bond, leave it there.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Let matter carry a decision the mind keeps reopening.

GAME MOVE
Start at Picture Safe; next, Name Responsibility. Complete Physical ends the useful part.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Picture Safe — Picture or select a safe symbol for what you are relinquishing.
2. Choose Transformation — Choose a transformation that fits: fold, seal, store, shred, bury where lawful, or dissolve safely.
3. Name Responsibility — Name what is ending and what responsibility remains.
4. Complete Physical — Complete the physical change once.

FINISH MOVE — Let Complete Physical be enough.

Notice this in Change The Object, Mark The Release: let matter carry a decision the mind keeps reopening. Then stop at Complete Physical.

rituals.title: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON
rituals.name: TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON
rituals.hook: Action avoidance is the cue; use Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon. Test this: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.recognition_cue: Action avoidance is the cue; use Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon. Test this: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.goal: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.mission: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.challenge: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.immediate_need: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.game_move: Run Ask Far; let Park Scenario work. Close with Decide Information.
rituals.unique_game_move: Run Ask Far; let Park Scenario work. Close with Decide Information.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Action avoidance is the cue; use Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon. Test this: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.

GAME MOVE
Run Ask Far; let Park Scenario work. Close with Decide Information.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Far — Ask how far ahead consequences can meaningfully alter today’s move: tonight, one week, six months.
2. Imagine Line — Imagine a line at that horizon.
3. Park Scenario — Park every scenario beyond it unless it changes a present safety or commitment fact.
4. Decide Information — Decide using information inside the line.

FINISH MOVE — Decide Information is your cue to stop.
rituals.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon asks one question: can you not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision?. Leave at Decide Information.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Far → Imagine Line → Park Scenario → Decide Information
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Extend the horizon for hard to undo actions or long-term obligations.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
rituals.safety_notes:

rituals.hook: Your first interpretation does not get automatic ownership of the event. MEANING ON HOLD waits for facts before granting a story authority.
rituals.recognition_cue: Your first interpretation does not get automatic ownership of the event. MEANING ON HOLD waits for facts before granting a story authority.

rituals.immediate_need: Meaning must wait for independent witnesses.
rituals.game_move: Run Hold Event; let Name Meaning work. Close at Assign Narrowest; do not restart.
rituals.unique_game_move: Run Hold Event; let Name Meaning work. Close at Assign Narrowest; do not restart.

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Meaning must wait for independent witnesses.

GAME MOVE
Run Hold Event; let Name Meaning work. Close at Assign Narrowest; do not restart.
rituals.play_the_loop:
1. Hold Event — Hold the event without explaining it.
2. Find Facts — Find three facts from different channels—what was said, what was observed, what occurred over time.
3. Name Meaning — Until all three exist, Name every meaning temporary.
4. Assign Narrowest — Then assign the narrowest meaning supported.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Wait For The Whole Body Answer gives Posture–mood locking a boundary. One job: Some experience forms before it can be explained.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Some experience forms before it can be explained.

GAME MOVE
Begin Bring Mind; hinge on Check Whether. Leave It Raw lands; leave it.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Bring Mind — Bring the issue to mind lightly, then pause verbal analysis.
2. Ask Body — Ask the body, ‘What is the whole of this like?’ Wait for an image, phrase, posture, or global texture.
3. Check Whether — Check whether it fits by noticing a small inner yes, no, or shift.
4. Leave It Raw — Do not improve the answer.

FINISH MOVE — Let Leave It Raw be enough.

End the inquiry if bodily attention creates panic, numbness, or feeling unreal or disconnected.

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Not This, Still Here loosens Dissociation drift. Aim: Remove identities without attacking experience.

Take Body; keep Keep Perspective literal. Stop at Rest Unlabelled.

1. Body — Notice body, sensation, thought, emotion, and role in turn.

items.play_the_loop:
1. Name Pattern — Name the recurring pattern in one line, including the trigger and usual response.
2. Find Misses — Find two occasions when the same kind of trigger produced no pattern or a clearly weaker version.
3. Compare Conditions — Compare the exceptions. Spot one shared condition that you can influence: timing, preparation, company, distance, information, or body care.
4. Transplant Edge — Place that condition into the next comparable situation and define what weaker would look like.

items.play_the_loop:
1. Stage Door — Choose the opening movements: open the file, place the tool, find the line, or position your hands. Keep it under ten seconds.
2. Dry Launch — Perform that sequence once without producing work. Stop at the edge of action; this is the dry launch.
3. Full Reset — Return your hands or screen to neutral exactly once. Do not improve the plan or add another rehearsal.
4. Live Entry — Repeat the same sequence and continue straight into thirty seconds of real work.

The first start can be rehearsal; the second one becomes real. Once visible, Run The Start Gate Twice can end at Live Entry.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
For Automatic-pattern blindness, open Difference Inside One Field. Work toward: Diversity need not become division.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Diversity need not become division.

GAME MOVE
Contrasting frames it; Include Shared tests it. Do not pass Let Difference.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Contrasting — Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence.
2. Hold Distinct — Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
3. Include Shared — Then include the shared field in which both are present.
4. Let Difference — Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Let Difference, then return to your day.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.

GAME MOVE
Start at Say Alarm; next, Find Weight. Stopping line: Keep Signal.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.

FINISH MOVE — Keep Signal is your cue to stop.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
The practical win in Move The Heaviest Word: move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight. End at Keep Signal.
items.formula_flow: Say Alarm → Shift Stress → Find Weight → Keep Signal
items.safety:
PAUSE
Use silent emphasis if speaking is unsafe; stop for voice strain, breathing difficulty, or rising panic.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.play_the_loop:
1. Picture Safe — Picture or select a safe symbol for what you are relinquishing.

4. Complete Physical — Complete the physical change once.

items.hook: Action avoidance is the cue; use Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon. Test this: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.

items.unique_game_move: Run Ask Far; let Park Scenario work. Close with Decide Information.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Action avoidance is the cue; use Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon. Test this: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.

GAME MOVE
Run Ask Far; let Park Scenario work. Close with Decide Information.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Ask Far — Ask how far ahead consequences can meaningfully alter today’s move: tonight, one week, six months.
2. Imagine Line — Imagine a line at that horizon.
3. Park Scenario — Park every scenario beyond it unless it changes a present safety or commitment fact.
4. Decide Information — Decide using information inside the line.

FINISH MOVE — Decide Information is your cue to stop.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Today’S Furthest Useful Horizon asks one question: can you not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision?. Leave at Decide Information.
items.formula_flow: Ask Far → Imagine Line → Park Scenario → Decide Information

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

GOAL
Meaning must wait for independent witnesses.

GAME MOVE
Run Hold Event; let Name Meaning work. Close at Assign Narrowest; do not restart.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Hold Event — Hold the event without explaining it.
2. Find Facts — Find three facts from different channels—what was said, what was observed, what occurred over time.
3. Name Meaning — Until all three exist, Name every meaning temporary.
4. Assign Narrowest — Then assign the narrowest meaning supported.

GOAL
A vague fear cannot lose because it never defines a result.

GAME MOVE
Keep Rewrite Prediction small; move through Define. Let Set Review finish.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Sharpen Forecast — Sharpen the prediction with who, what visible event, exact time window, location, and clear threshold.
2. Define — Define the sign of the event not happening.
3. Set Review — Set a review date and refuse to score the forecast before then.

FINISH MOVE — Complete Set Review, then return to your day.

items.name: TURN DOWN THE DOMINANT CHANNEL
items.hook: Turn Down The Dominant Channel changes the angle on Context neglect. Test this: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.

items.challenge: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.
items.immediate_need: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.
items.game_move: Identify Loudest to Reduce Brightness; no rewind. Close with Date Clothing.
items.unique_game_move: Identify Loudest to Reduce Brightness; no rewind. Close with Date Clothing.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Evidence distortion & selective thinking

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Turn Down The Dominant Channel changes the angle on Context neglect. Test this: A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix.

GAME MOVE
Identify Loudest to Reduce Brightness; no rewind. Close with Date Clothing.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Identify Loudest — Spot the loudest recall channel—image, sound, touch, smell.
2. Reduce Brightness — Reduce its brightness, volume, proximity, or texture slightly.
3. Date Clothing — At the same time strengthen neutral context such as room layout, date, clothing, or distant sound.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Turn Down The Dominant Channel did its job if: a memory can feel present because one sense owns the mix. Leave at Date Clothing.
items.formula_flow: Identify Loudest → Reduce Brightness → Date Clothing
items.safety:
PAUSE
Do not manipulate testimony or use this when precise recall is legally important.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.hook: When boundary confusion starts steering, Set The Limit Before The Next Test narrows the problem to this: Decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.

items.game_move: Count Pattern opens; Link Consequence changes the angle. Stop at Follow Contract.
items.unique_game_move: Count Pattern opens; Link Consequence changes the angle. Stop at Follow Contract.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Boundaries & over-responsibility

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
When boundary confusion starts steering, Set The Limit Before The Next Test narrows the problem to this: Decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.

GAME MOVE
Count Pattern opens; Link Consequence changes the angle. Stop at Follow Contract.
items.play_the_loop:
1. Count Pattern — Define the behaviour in terms a camera could Keep.
2. Set Threshold — Choose the count, duration, or date that will Notice the limit.
3. Link Consequence — Attach one consequence under your control, such as ending the call, leaving, or changing access.
4. Follow Contract — If the threshold is crossed, follow the contract once without holding a motive trial.

FINISH MOVE — Follow Contract closes the round.
items.win_reward:
WIN SIGNAL
Set The Limit Before The Next Test closes with Follow Contract; what matters is decide the enforcement rule while the room is calm.
items.formula_flow: Count Pattern → Set Threshold → Link Consequence → Follow Contract
items.safety:
PAUSE
Leave immediately instead of counting repetitions when there is intimidation, violence, or immediate danger.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
